standard.title: Discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.description: use play, imagination, arts knowledge, processes and/or skills to discover possibilities and develop ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior Drama curriculum. Students bring exploratory play using body, voice and materials; early curiosity about imaginative scenarios.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use play, imagination and available arts skills and materials to discover possibilities and develop ideas for arts-making.

nodes.label: Exploring through play and materials
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use play — with materials, voice, or movement — to discover possible ideas or actions.
nodes.minimum_width: Student engages in purposeful exploration: trying out a material, voice quality, or movement to see what it might express.
nodes.typical_width: Students use a range of materials (rough/smooth textures, objects, clothing items) and modes (voice, movement, gesture) in open-ended exploration; they notice and name something they discover.
wider: Students respond to music or soundscapes through movement, discovering expressive possibilities in their body
Students explore how geometric shapes suggest movement or character — improvising actions that trace or embody a shape
nodes.hinge_reason: If students are not yet engaging in exploratory play — just watching or randomly handling materials — they have no raw material from which to develop ideas; the 'develop ideas' move collapses.

response_modes.reason: Offer varied entry points: sound, texture, image, movement. Students who don't engage with one mode often connect strongly with another — breadth of invitation is the remedy here.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The range of sensory and imaginative entry points at Foundation is very wide; students who explore across multiple modes build a richer expressive vocabulary earlier.
success_criteria: Student engages in purposeful exploration with at least one mode (materials, voice, or movement)
Student notices and can name or show something they discovered through play

nodes.label: Developing an idea from exploration
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can extend an initial discovery into a developing idea — asking 'what if?' or 'what next?' to push the play further.
nodes.minimum_width: Student makes at least one 'what if?' move — e.g. changes a voice quality, adds a movement, or repurposes a material in a new way.
nodes.typical_width: Students extend their exploratory play by imagining characters, situations or possibilities ('What would happen if...?'); they try at least two variations and choose one to develop further.
wider: Students use inquiry questions about a story or image ('What is happening? What will happen next?') to generate new imaginative directions
Students document a step in their making process using a digital photo or drawing, creating a simple record of how the idea developed
Students collaborate with a partner to build on each other's ideas in dramatic play

response_modes.reason: Teacher prompts ('What else could happen?', 'What if your character could fly?') scaffold the move from random play to intentional idea-development.

success_criteria: Student makes at least one variation or extension on an initial discovery
Student can describe or show what they were exploring and one thing they tried
